Definition: of Hebrew origin (H2608); Annas (i.e. G367), an Israelite:--Annas.
BiblicalUsage: Annas is the high priest who had Jesus brought before him first, the father-in-law of Caiaphas, and the power behind the priesthood for years. John names him in the trial, Luke names him at the start of John the Baptist's ministry, and Acts names him among the rulers who threatened Peter and John.
TheologicalSignificance: Annas shows me how power can outlive office: he was no longer high priest, yet Jesus was brought to him first. I believe the trial of Jesus exposes every kind of corruption, and I hold that no council of men can condemn what God has appointed.
RelatedPeople: Annas; Caiaphas; Simon Peter; John the Apostle
RelatedEvents: Jesus Before the Sanhedrin; Peter and John Before the Sanhedrin
